contract.application_relevance: Carry a read-session bookmark between application components while independent sessions retain their own state.

cleanup.finally: For every claimed resource independently, DROP TABLE IF EXISTS and read sqlite_schema by exact name; require null and no cleanup errors. Deduplicate alias identities by owning only the canonical binding.
cleanup.on_stall: The separately reviewed adapter must enforce the total request deadline, stop only the owned invocation and, if request cancellation cannot be proved, the owned celld process group; preserve evidence then discard only its disposable store. No cleanup success may be inferred after timeout.
cleanup.preflight: For each declared physical identity/table, SELECT sqlite_schema by exact bound name and require absence before claiming ownership. Refuse pre-existing objects and never drop them. A fresh isolated store and serial runner remain mandatory.
cleanup.wave_end: Stop the owned celld group and discard its disposable store even if every finally check succeeds.

contract.distinctness: Session-local query-bookmark lifecycle and resume, explicitly celld source behavior with no replica/consistency-order claim.
fixed_finite_trace: Create first-primary and default sessions; require null initial bookmarks.
Read through the first session, require celld:primary and unchanged other session.
Create a new session from the returned bookmark and read exact data again.
contract.intent: Carry a read-session bookmark between application components while independent sessions retain their own state.
limits_of_evidence: Source-backed assertion candidate only; zero execution, zero review acceptance.
No cross-node, restart, durability-loss, fault, rollback, malformed-input, authorization or guarded G/N/P/J122 claim.
Successful batch dependencies do not establish concurrent-observer atomicity.
Finite source traces do not substitute for an independently enforced outer deadline and owned teardown.

assertions: new constraint sessions start without completed-query bookmarks
session prepare reads its bound database
successful session query advances to the stable primary bookmark
one session query does not mutate another session bookmark
new session retains the supplied prior bookmark
resumed session reads exact committed data
completed reads keep the stable opaque primary token
oracle.claim: Constraints begin with null bookmarks; each successful _query changes only that session bookmark to the constant celld:primary; supplied bookmark is retained initially.
executable_assertion_source: c.eq([session.getBookmark(),other.getBookmark()], [null,null], "new constraint sessions start without completed-query bookmarks");
c.eq(await c.first(session.prepare(`SELECT n FROM ${t} WHERE id=1`), "session read"), {n:8}, "session prepare reads its bound database");
c.eq(session.getBookmark(), "celld:primary", "successful session query advances to the stable primary bookmark");
c.eq(other.getBookmark(), null, "one session query does not mutate another session bookmark");
c.eq(resumed.getBookmark(), "celld:primary", "new session retains the supplied prior bookmark");
c.eq(await c.first(resumed.prepare(`SELECT n FROM ${t} WHERE id=1`), "resumed session read"), {n:8}, "resumed session reads exact committed data");
c.eq(resumed.getBookmark(), "celld:primary", "completed reads keep the stable opaque primary token");
oracle.qualification: All expectations are against the exact pinned direct celld source. Metadata resets, primary service markers, stable bookmark, exec counts and database-name fallback are deliberately not universal Cloudflare claims. No runtime or workerd comparison was performed.

schedule.ordering: Every public dispatch is awaited before the next; no overlapping requests, timers, retries or random schedules. prepare/bind/session constructors/bookmark access are synchronous local operations.

contract.surface: public env D1 binding APIs only
